prompt:
Now we are merging two PDDL domains into one domain. Please help judge whether two PDDL operators are equivalent.

domain_1:
    action in domain_1: (:action kettle_transform_to_fur_badger :parameters (?t - entity ?k - item) :precondition (and (night) (located ?k jhosiu) (has ?t ?k)) :effect (and (furred ?k) (badger_form ?k) (four_legged ?k)))
    predicates explaination in domain_1: {'(badger_form ?i - item)': "item ?i is in the state 'badger form'; used as effect of kettle_transform_to_badger, precondition of call_novices, precondition of kettle_jump_and_fly, effect of kettle_transform_to_fur_badger, precondition of kettle_revert_shape, effect of kettle_revert_shape", '(four_legged ?i - item)': "item ?i is in the state 'four legged'; used as effect of kettle_transform_to_fur_badger, effect of kettle_revert_shape", '(furred ?i - item)': "item ?i is in the state 'furred'; used as effect of kettle_transform_to_fur_badger, precondition of kettle_revert_shape, effect of kettle_revert_shape", '(has ?e - entity ?i - item)': "relation 'has' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?i is a item; used as precondition of receive_payment, effect of receive_payment, precondition of spend_money_on_drink, effect of spend_money_on_drink, precondition of trade_assets_for_money, effect of trade_assets_for_money, effect of take_item_and_hide, precondition of hang_kettle", '(located ?obj - object ?loc - location)': "relation 'located' holds; arguments: ?obj is a object, ?loc is a location; used as effect of call_novices, precondition of kettle_transform_to_fur_badger", '(night)': "the state 'night' holds; used as precondition of kettle_transform_to_fur_badger"}

domain_2:
    action in domain_2: (:action audience_demand_shake_cloak_for_pig :parameters (?audience ?performer - entity ?cloak - item) :effect (audience_demands_shake_cloak ?audience ?performer ?cloak))
    predicates explaination in domain_2: {'(audience_demands_shake_cloak ?audience - entity ?performer - entity ?cloak - item)': "relation 'audience demands shake cloak' holds; arguments: ?audience is a entity, ?performer is a entity, ?cloak is a item; used as effect of audience_demand_shake_cloak_for_pig"}

Please judge whether the two operators can be merged into one action based on following rules:
(1) If the two actions have the same name, they MUST be merged into one action;
(2) If the two actions are semantically equivalent (although they may differ in preconditions and effects), merge them. Genrally, you need to union their preconditions and effects.
(3) Note that do NOT merge two actions if the logic becomes more complex after merging. For example, do NOT use "or", "when" to union two actions (about their preconditions and effects). Namely NOT too general. 
(4) Do NOT invent any predicate.
(5) If you decide to merge two actions. You can invent new action name. But the new name must be reasonable according to the whole predicates in the action.
    For example: if the action expresses the meaning of "pick some object from drawer" according to the predicates in preconditions and effects, just name it like "pick_from_drawer", instead of "pick_from_container", etc.
(6) Keep the given PDDL style. Please use PDDL 1.0 and do NOT use Conditional Effects like "when", etc.
(7) Note the number of brackets in the PDDL format.

Your output should include four part:
(1) reasoning: your analysis process;
(2) merge_flag: whether the two operators can be merged into one;
(3) new_operator_name: if equivalent, output the new operator name (in one of the given operator or a new invented operator).
(4) new_operator: if equivalent, output the new operator in PDDL format.

If "merge_flag" is false, the "new_operator_name" and "new_operator" parts are null.

Your output should be in JSON format like below:
{
    "reasoning": "your analysis process",
    "merge_flag": true,
    "new_operator_name": "open_door",
    "new_operator": "(:action open_door \n :parameters (?r ?d) \n :precondition (and (hand_free ?r)) \n :effect (and (is_open ?d)))"
}

Do NOT output any strange symbols like "\".
